top.title: Trump admin still won't let Wi-Fi giant TP-Link sell its latest routers in US
top.description: TP-Link, which may be the top provider of wireless routers for US homes and small businesses, isn't allowed to sell its latest Wi-Fi routers in the US. The Trump administration imposed a sweeping ban on foreign-made consumer routers in March 2026, and TP-Link hasn't been able to obtain an exemption. The rules prevent the import or sale of all new router models that are manufactured, assembled, designed, or developed outside the US. The Trump administration has control over which router makers receive special permission to import and sell new products through a waiver-review process involving the Federal Communications Commission, the Department of Defense, and the Department of Homeland Security. While some of its competitors have obtained exemptions to the ban, TP-Link appears to be having a hard time making its case to government officials. Its routers approved before the March 2026 ban remain available for sale in the US, but its newly released Wi-Fi 8 routers cannot be imported or sold. Read full article Comments

top.title: Tiger Woods ‘Still Fully Believes’ He Can ‘Beat Anyone’ at Golf Despite ‘Dealing With So Much Pain’
top.description: ZUMAPRESS.com / MEGA Tiger Woods wants to be a champion — and anything less is going to be very hard for him to accept as he prepares to return to the world of professional golf at the Hero World Challenge tournament in the Bahamas in December, a source tells Globe . “Even with everything that’s happened, Tiger still fully believes he can, and will, beat anyone on the course,” reveals the source. “It’s a great mindset, but it’s also worrying because a lot of people think he’s setting the bar too high.” Over the years, Woods, 50, has sustained several injuries, per AP , including a ruptured Achilles tendon and ACL, and undergone multiple back surgeries. As Globe previously reported, the 82-time PGA Tour champion also recently completed a stint in rehab in Switzerland after rolling over his Land Rover in Jupiter, Florida, on March 27. He was charged with a DUI but pleaded no contest to a lesser charge that will see his driver’s license suspended for five years. “His body just isn’t what it used to be,” admits the source. “He’s still dealing with so much pain. Everyone is telling him that just making this comeback is incredible, regardless of whether he wins or not, but Tiger doesn’t want to hear that.” Instagram/Tiger Woods Girlfriend Vanessa Trump is “very supportive, but she also doesn’t want to see him overdo it or get down on himself if things don’t go his way,” says Globe ‘s source. At the same time, “she’s also got to protect her own peace,” the source adds. In late October, Donald Trump Jr. ‘s ex-wife, 48, announced on Instagram that she is officially cancer-free after undergoing treatment for cancer earlier this year. “She’s been through so much with her health,” notes the source. “She needs her life to be as stress-free as possible and that is going to be hard if Tiger’s putting all this pressure on himself.” Read More From Globe Professor Who Claims His Affair With a Student Was Like 'Fatal Attraction' Accused of Sexual Assault Man Named Captain America Accused of Murdering Coworker, Demanding Money From His Girlfriend Kentucky Teacher Charged With 30 New Counts of Abuse, Human Trafficking of Minors After Prior Arrests This story Tiger Woods ‘Still Fully Believes’ He Can ‘Beat Anyone’ at Golf Despite ‘Dealing With So Much Pain’ first appeared on Globe . top.title: GB's Davis Cup-winning captain ends 17-year stint
top.description: Leon Smith guided Great Britain to their first Davis Cup title in 79 years [Getty Images] Great Britain's Davis Cup-winning captain Leon Smith is stepping down after almost 17 years in the role. Smith guided the British men's team to Davis Cup victory in 2015 - the nation's first win in the event since 1936. The 50-year-old Scot will leave his role after next week's Finals in Bologna, where he is hoping to create "another special memory" by leading the team to the title once again. Smith's successor has not yet been appointed, but the Lawn Tennis Association (LTA) has spoken to potential candidates and hopes to announce the new captain as soon as possible. Former world number one Andy Murray, who was instrumental in Britain's 2015 victory, is not believed to be interested in the role at this time. "It has been an enormous privilege to lead the team for so many years, and I feel now is the right time, both for me personally and for the team moving forwards," Smith said. "Winning the Davis Cup in 2015 will always be one of the proudest moments of my career, but there are countless other experiences and memories that I'll cherish forever." With Smith picking the team and creating a tight bond between the group, Murray was the driving force on the court as he won all eight of his singles matches in the victorious campaign. Murray was coached by Smith as a child and said winning the Davis Cup together was "one of the proudest moments" of his career. "He did a great job of bringing everyone together and making sure we all felt we had a part to play. He got the best out of us that year," three-time Grand Slam champion Murray said. "I've obviously known Leon a long time, I think the most fun we had together was when I was playing Davis Cup and Leon was on the bench. I'm really glad we got to share those moments. "I wish Leon all the best as he steps down, and good luck to the new captain." top.title: Puka Nacua faces NFL ‘banishment’ under suspension guidelines
top.description: Before Week 11 of the 2026-27 NFL season kicked off, the league announced that one of its biggest stars, Puka Nacua , has been suspended for three games for violating the personal conduct policy . The timing of the suspension turned out to be beneficial to the Rams and Nacua. Nacua is currently on injured reserve, so he was set to miss the next three games regardless of his status with the league. The All-Pro pass catcher will be eligible for reinstatement on Monday, December 14 . However, Nacua’s suspension does come with a strong warning from the league. NFL Insider Tom Pelissero shared further details about what any future violation or “failure to satisfy conditions of the diversion program” could entail. According to Pelissero, if Nacua does not comply with the diversion program or finds himself in trouble down the road, it “could lead to additional discipline, up to and including banishment .” MORE: Stephen A. top.title: Does Villanova Basketball Have A Backcourt Problem?
top.description: Villanova has played just five games and there have been some strong reactions to the overall performance. Is it too early to make judgments and overreact? The answer is no. When a team rebuilds a roster that cost plenty of money, results are expected right away. Let’s not forget, in five games, Villanova has played two real opponents and have lost both games. With Michigan and Kansas coming up, it could get uglier if the team does not clean up. The main issue that needs to get cleaned up is in the backcourt. The point guard position has not been good enough. Elijah Crawford has made some plays early this season, particularly against Notre Dame in the opener, but it is becoming clear that he has not been good enough. Is it quick to say that he is not good enough to play in the Big East? That is yet to be seen, but the early returns have not been positive. Crawford was a big-time recruit coming out of high school before going to BYU and then UIC. He is not going to be asked to score much for Villanova. He is averaging six assists through five games with 2.2 turnovers. It is important that the team has a ball handler to set the offense up with what should be an improved frontcourt and Tyler Perkins on the perimeter. Darryl Simmons was also added this offseason. He has been a strong shooter from deep during his career. This is a valuable skillset off the bench. Simmons is already dealing with an injury that kept him sidelined against Pitt. We’re not going to mention how both Acaden Lewis and Bryce Lindsay are off to strong starts for their respective teams this season. We’re not going to do it. But if we were to, how different would it look? There is some time before Big East play begins. That is what really matters for Villanova. But to compete this year, the backcourt must get figured out.

top.title: Tottenham Hotspur vs. Ipswich Town Premier League Preview
top.description: It was a shockingly positive October for Tottenham Hotspur with a draw at Old Trafford and three wins to follow, including the amazing result at Stamford Bridge. Of course, that naturally led to a depressingly flat performance against Leeds right before the break, which sent Spurs back to the bottom half of the table, though thankfully out of the relegation zone as has been the case for much of the past two seasons. Back in action, Tottenham gets three matches against teams below it in the table before a home North London Derby the first weekend of December. This run begins with a visit from Ipswich Town, who sits joint-13th with 11 points through 10 contests; all three of its wins this season came in the first six matchweeks, with just two points taken across the most recent four fixtures. Spurs disappointed against Leeds, but really must be taking all three points on Saturday. With back-to-back wins at home for the first time in ages, the Lane should be fully behind this squad against an overmatched opponent. Roberto De Zerbi’s group must take things one match at a time, but the next three matches feel like a quite important stretch. Match Details Date : Saturday, November 21 Time : 10:00 am ET, 3:00 pm UK Location : Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, London TV : USA Network (US) Prior to Ipswich’s brief return to the Championship, these two sides split the contests in 2024/25, with the road team claiming each victory. In North London, the Tractor Boys scored twice in the first half, and a Rodrigo Bentancur consolation was not enough to prevent Ipswich from earning its first win. The reverse fixture saw four Spurs goals at Portman Road: a Brennan Johnson first-half brace, plus tallies from Djed Spence and Dejan Kulusevski to firmly put it away. Optimistically on the rise The rise in the table, the stringing together of wins, and the conquest over Chelsea all point to the tangible ways this team is making progress, and much of this felt overdue after Spurs kept putting together pieces of strong performances without being able to fully earn the result. The underlying metrics still see the club as squarely mid-table, but the trend is absolutely in the right direction. On top of this, optimism rises with the squad list. James Maddison, Savio, and Lucas Bergvall are among those who are coming back and should make a substantial impact in the lineup. With Kulusevski and Mohammed Kudus already available, De Zerbi will have far more attacking options now at his disposal, even with Mathys Tel and Xavi Simons out. This combination of form and personnel should have Tottenham’s confidence growing every week. Contrast that with the visitors who are winless in four and have only taken points from teams who are currently in the bottom eight spots of the table. Call me foolish, but this sets up well for Spurs, as the home side should be able to break down an opposing defense that has allowed the second-most goals this season. top.title: #PostPulpit mailbag: What’s wrong with the Patriots defense?
top.description: Behind back-to-back blowout losses and losing Drake Maye to injury , the New England Patriots season has quickly derailed over the last two weeks. Now, they have plenty questions to answers after a much needed bye week. So, let’s get into some of those in this week’s edition of the #PostPulpit Mailbag. What has gone so wrong with the defense? They’re relatively healthy and have a lot of the same personnel as last year. Kuhr did a great job last year and really earned the official promotion to DC. So what happened? Along the same lines, do you think Gonzo is really the type of player who, now that he’s gotten his payday, is going to sit on his laurels for the remainder of his career? – TDDsDad Is the defense’s biggest problem the square peg or round hole – scheme doesn’t fit players or players don’t fit scheme – spyponder90 The Patriots defense has a litany of problems right now. Here’s how we’d break them down: Zone coverage: Statistically, the Patriots are the worst zone coverage team in football, ranking dead last in both EPA and passer rating allowed in zone coverage. Defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr was a step ahead of opposing offenses earlier this season with his disguises in the secondary, but teams have caught on while New England’s defensive backs have failed to live up to their potential. Some of the issues in zone coverage also tie back to the pass rush. The Patriots rank 20th in the league in four-man pressure rate, giving opposing quarterbacks time to find the voids in coverage. To generate pressure, New England has had to blitz, which then leaves more space for the offense to attack with at least one defender taken out of coverage — as seen on Jahmyr Gibbs’ 50-yard reception last week. Man coverage: The logical follow-up would be to play more man coverage, especially with New England’s talented cover corners. The Patriots already rank near the top of the league in man coverage rate, but no team can rely on man coverage for the majority of a game for several reasons. Without an effective changeup, opposing offenses have game-planned for man coverage and exploit it with beaters such as stacks and bunch formations. On top of that, the talented cover corners have again not been playing to their potential. Effort/tackling: New England is not a poor tackling team by the numbers, but the defense often doesn’t appear to be rallying to the football — a concern when Mike Vrabel has made effort and finish his No. 1 non-negotiable . top.title: Shannon Sharpe thinks he knows ‘the main reason’ why LeBron James left the Lakers
top.description: Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images LeBron James left the Los Angeles Lakers in the summer of 2026 after eight years with the franchise. The 41-year-old joined the Philadelphia 76ers in the off-season, and he seems to be having a great time there. The Lakers are doing well without him too. Since his summer move, there have been several theories about why James decided to leave the Lakers. Shannon Sharpe has now had his say on what he thinks happened. Shannon Sharpe says LeBron James left the Lakers because he was disrespected James has been one of the biggest names in the NBA for a long time, and when he joined the Los Angeles Lakers, many expected them to dominate. However, the Lakers won just one NBA Championship with The King in his eight years there, which is one of the reasons why things turned a bit sour in the end. Some fans wanted James gone because they believed that Luka Doncic was their real star and would take them to the next level on his own. Sharpe believes that was one of the reasons why James felt disrespected and decided to leave. He said on the Nightcap show : “I think the main reason LeBron left the Lakers is that he felt like they didn’t respect him anymore. “He felt like, ‘Look, I understand Luka’s better, but y’all just blatantly disregarded what I’ve done for you guys the last eight years. Do y’all not remember what transpired the last couple of years Kobe was here? “‘Because Kobe was hurt a lot, and do you remember when Kobe retired, that 60-point game? What y’all did in ’16 and ’17. Do y’all remember that? And then for you to have this kind of laissez-faire attitude, it’s just like, you know what, y’all don’t really appreciate it.’ “And he heard it: ‘We don’t need LeBron. We don’t want LeBron. We got Luka.'” LeBron James’ summer departure has worked out for everyone There was a big debate in the summer following James’ departure from Los Angeles. Some were of the opinion that the Lakers would struggle this season, while others believed that The King’s new team, the Philadelphia 76ers, would have problems because of him. However, when you look at the records of the two teams, they are pretty similar. Of course, the debate about James and the Lakers will go on until the end of the season and perhaps even beyond that point. However, we think people should just accept that his departure was the best move for all parties involved and move on. top.title: Ben Shelton completes feat only Rafael Nadal can match this century after latest win at the ATP Finals
top.description: Ben Shelton broke new ground in his career by reaching the semifinals of the ATP Finals for the first time. After Arthur Fils lost the first set of his third and final group stage match against Alexander Zverev on Thursday, Shelton ‘s spot in the final four was confirmed. The 24-year-old American had beaten Rafael Jodar in straight sets earlier in the day to boost his chances of advancing at the prestigious year-end tournament. Photo by Pascal von Büren/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty Images Ben Shelton matches Rafael Nadal after advancing at the ATP Finals With his triumph, Shelton became the youngest American since Andy Roddick in 2004 to reach the semifinals of the ATP Finals. He also became the first left-hander other than Rafael Nadal to do so this century. Nadal made the semifinals six times and advanced to the championship match twice: in 2010 and 2013. The legendary Spaniard never managed to win the title, however, despite making 11 appearances. Shelton qualified for the ATP Finals for the first time last year, but was knocked out in the round-robin stage. He went winless in his debut campaign, winning just one set throughout the run against Felix Auger-Aliassime. This time around, Shelton has tallied a record of 2-1 in the group stage, having beaten Fils and Jodar but losing to Zverev. The loss to the German was his seventh straight in their head-to-head and first since the US Open final. Photo by Sona Maleterova/Getty Images Ben Shelton’s semifinal opponent at the ATP Finals in Turin After finishing second in the John McEnroe group, Shelton will face the winner of the Ivan Lendl group, Carlos Alcaraz, on Monday. Alcaraz secured his spot atop his group after beating Daniil Medvedev and Frances Tiafoe, both in straight sets. Shelton has faced Alcaraz five times on the ATP Tour and has only come out on top against him once. Shelton’s sole victory in the head-to-head came in the quarterfinals of this year’s US Open, where he emerged victorious in a five-set thriller. Alcaraz has since earned revenge by beating Shelton in the Paris Masters final to extend his lead in the rivalry to 4-1. Their upcoming clash at the ATP Finals will be their third on an indoor hard court.

The state of the New York roster reflects the superteam transformation that took place during the 2023 offseason, as well as the franchise’s subsequent championship-or-bust approach to every season, where the drafting and development of young players has been sacrificed in favor acquiring stars or veterans. It all, of course, paid off in 2024, when the Liberty captured that long-sought first championship. After finishing at No. 8 in the standings in 2026, New York now clings to their championship contender identity, as last offseason’s attempted refresh failed, leaving the currently head coach-less Liberty with questions about how to build a roster that capable of achieving the organization’s championship ambitions. Thank you, Coach DeMarco. pic.twitter.com/tbxe0MDInT — New York Liberty (@nyliberty) November 3, 2026 A singular middle-of-the-first-round draft pick doesn’t project to do much to alter the Liberty’s immediate future. And as tons of offseason activity will occur before draft night, there’s a decent chance New York, once again, might not be making this pick. nigeria.title: Court Rejects Atiku’s Bid to Tender Fresh Evidence In Suit Seeking Tinubu’s Disqualification
nigeria.description: Justice Inyang Ekwo of the Federal High Court in Abuja has dismissed an application by former Vice President and the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, to present fresh evidence in his suit seeking to prevent President Bola Tinubu from contesting the 2027 presidential election over allegations of forgery of his National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) discharge certificate. The judge held that the time allowed by law to present evidence in a pre-election suit was 14 days, in line with Section 285(9) of the 1999 Constitution. Justice Ekwo agreed with Tinubu and the other defendants that allowing Atiku to introduce fresh evidence would alter the nature of the original case and violate the provisions of the Constitution. In his ruling on Atiku’s application to amend the originating summons in the suit against Tinubu, the All Progressives Congress (APC) and the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), the judge held that the former vice president attempted to mislead the court by claiming that the proposed amendment would not introduce fresh issues. Justice Ekwo said that, after carefully examining the application, the court found that the ADC presidential candidate sought to substitute existing evidence with new evidence which, if allowed, would circumvent Section 285(9) of the Constitution, which requires such evidence to be presented within 14 days. A man walks past the Federal High Court premises in Abuja, on April 22, 2026. (Photo by LIGHT ORIYE TAMUNOTONYE / AFP) According to the judge, allowing Atiku to introduce fresh evidence through the back door would amount to a fundamental injustice against the defendants. Meanwhile, following an agreement among the lawyers, the judge fixed December 2 for the hearing of the substantive suit. Atiku had told the court that he needed to make substantial amendments to his case challenging Tinubu’s eligibility to participate in the 2027 presidential election. In the main suit, Atiku and the ADC asked Justice Ekwo to disqualify Tinubu and the APC from the 2027 presidential election. They challenged the authenticity of Tinubu’s NYSC discharge certificate submitted to INEC by the APC. The plaintiffs, who sued the president, the APC and INEC as the first to third defendants, respectively, in an originating summons marked FHC/ABJ/CS/1888/2026, alleged that the APC submitted a forged NYSC discharge certificate belonging to the president to INEC. nigeria.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, November 20, 2026
nigeria.description: The Nigerian naira continued to face downward pressure against the United States dollar across both the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM) and the parallel market on Friday, November 20, 2026, driven by tightening foreign exchange supply and rising end-of-year seasonal demand. Official Market Performance Real-time interbank spot tracking at the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market placed the US dollar at ₦1,352.54 during early morning trading on Friday, following an opening rate of ₦1,351.86 and an intraday peak of ₦1,355.31. This early session trading follows Thursday’s official Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) volume-weighted benchmark, which saw the naira depreciate to a four-month low. According to official CBN data for the November 19 trading session, the NFEM weighted average rate settled at ₦1,376.58 per dollar, while the indicative closing rate rose to ₦1,388.00 per dollar from ₦1,379.99 recorded on Wednesday. Intraday interbank transactions on Thursday were conducted between a low of ₦1,370.00 and a high of ₦1,397.00 per dollar. Despite the depreciation, market liquidity improved significantly, with NFEM interbank turnover surging by 59.13 percent to $800.31 million across 184 deals, up from $502.88 million the previous day. Parallel Market Rates In the parallel market, commonly referred to as the black market, the local currency weakened further as Bureau de Change (BDC) operators and street dealers in Lagos and Abuja quoted the US dollar at a selling rate of up to ₦1,468 per dollar on Friday morning, following Thursday’s close between ₦1,461 and ₦1,468. Buying rates among informal currency dealers hovered between ₦1,445 and ₦1,458 depending on transaction volume and location. With Thursday’s official closing benchmark at ₦1,388.00 and parallel market quotations reaching ₦1,468.00, the spread between the official and unofficial windows widened to ₦80.00 per dollar, compared to ₦70.01 recorded earlier in the week. Market Drivers and Reserve Outlook Since the end of October, when the naira closed at ₦1,346.00 in the official window and ₦1,373.00 in the parallel market, the currency has lost ₦42.00 and ₦95.00 in the respective segments. Meanwhile, Nigeria’s gross external reserves stood at $54.71 billion as of November 18, 2026, reflecting a moderation of $554 million from the October 27 peak of $55.26 billion. Financial analysts note that the recent divergence between both windows is largely fueled by heightened festive import demand, corporate obligations, and reduced autonomous foreign exchange inflows rather than a structural depletion of the country’s external reserves. entertainment.description: Five African destinations Nigerian passport holders can visit visa-free or with visa on arrival this Christmas holiday. Image: AI-generated. The group chat has the concerts, the dinners and the Detty December link-ups covered. But has anyone planned the getaway? Beyond the usual Lagos parties and end-of-year outings, there is a whole continent waiting to be explored, with sun-soaked beaches, wildlife safaris, exciting food scenes and cities with plenty of stories to tell. You do not have to spend weeks navigating embassy appointments and visa applications to make it happen, either. Several African countries offer Nigerian passport holders visa-free entry or visas on arrival, making a festive-season escape much easier to plan. Whether you are travelling solo, gathering your friends, taking the family along or joining a curated travel group, here are five destinations worth considering for your Christmas holiday. Kenya Imagine spotting lions and giraffes against a city skyline before breakfast, then catching an evening flight or train straight to the coast for fresh seafood by the Indian Ocean. That contrast is what makes Kenya such a rewarding December escape. Nairobi gives you immediate access to wildlife at Nairobi National Park and the Giraffe Centre alongside lively restaurants and art spaces in Westlands and Karen, while longer itineraries open up classic game drives in the Maasai Mara, views of Mount Kilimanjaro in Amboseli, and warm beach days in Diani or Watamu. Nigerian citizens enjoy visa-free entry for short stays of up to 60 days without needing a paid eTA, leaving more room in your budget for safaris and coastal stays. Rwanda Not everyone wants their year-end holiday to feel like a non-stop sprint, and Rwanda is built for travellers who prefer scenery, clean air, and an unhurried pace. Days in Kigali easily revolve around specialty coffee shops, contemporary art at Inema Arts Center, and a sobering, essential visit to the Kigali Genocide Memorial before you head out into the countryside. From the capital, you can track chimpanzees and walk above the trees in Nyungwe Forest, go on wildlife drives in Akagera National Park, or spend quiet afternoons along the shores of Lake Kivu. With 30-day visa-free entry for Nigerian passport holders, getting there is straightforward from start to finish. Mauritius Sometimes a proper Christmas break calls for leaving mainland schedules behind altogether for turquoise lagoons, catamaran cruises, and mountain trails. In Mauritius, you can base yourself around Grand Baie in the north for boat trips to Île aux Cerfs and lively beachside dinners, or head south-west toward Le Morne Brabant for coastal hikes and water sports. entertainment.title: Esther Adeyanju: This International Men’s Day, Let’s Make Room for Men’s Vulnerability
entertainment.description: “Men are not wired to show emotions.” A male friend once said to me during an argument. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Society has an interesting checklist for measuring a man’s success. A good job, a house, a car, a wife, children and financial stability. Preferably, all achieved before a certain age. But if a man struggles to achieve all these, is his life any less meaningful? Surely, a man’s worth cannot be reduced to his bank balance, job title or ability to convince everyone that he has everything under control. There must be room for men who are still becoming. entertainment.description: La Roche-Posay concluded its first Living Lab experience in Nigeria, welcoming Nigerian stakeholders to its opening party and three-day programme, held from 4 to 6 November 2026 at Oasis by The Five Palm, Victoria Island, Lagos. Inspired by the original Living Lab concept in Paris, the experience brought the science, research and expertise behind skincare closer to Nigerian consumers and healthcare professionals. It marked the brand’s first Living Lab in the country, creating a platform for more accessible conversations around skin health, dermatological innovation and everyday skincare. The experience opened with an exclusive session for healthcare professionals and invited guests before welcoming members of the public over the following two days. Each day featured three expert-led sessions exploring the role of dermatology and scientific research in advancing skin health, the wider impact of skin conditions on everyday life, and the importance of understanding product safety, tolerance and efficacy. The sessions brought together healthcare professionals and representatives from across Nigeria’s dermatological beauty and skincare community, encouraging knowledge-sharing and stronger connections between science, expertise and consumer education. Visitors explored five dedicated Innovation Corners showcasing La Roche-Posay’s Effaclar, Mela B3, Anthelios, Cicaplast and Lipikar ranges. Each space introduced visitors to specific skin concerns and the science behind the brand’s product formulations. Through interactive demonstrations and guided product experiences, guests gained a better understanding of different skin concerns and the role of targeted skincare in addressing them. At the Anthelios corner, visitors used a UV camera to see the effects of ultraviolet exposure and better understand the importance of sun protection. The Effaclar and Mela B3 spaces explored concerns including blemishes and hyperpigmentation, while the Cicaplast and Lipikar corners introduced visitors to approaches to caring for sensitive, damaged and dry skin. Beyond the Innovation Corners, visitors explored the Blue House, which presented La Roche-Posay’s history and commitment to dermatological innovation, and the Scars of Life Cinema. The cinema screened a 25-minute film exploring the physical and psychological realities of living with scars and scarring, including their impact on self-image and everyday life. The film also highlighted how Lipikar supports the care of skin affected by scarring, bringing attention to the importance of addressing both the visible and less visible experiences associated with skin conditions. Bringing together industry leaders, policymakers, corporate executives and other distinguished guests, the evening marked six years of WIEN’s advocacy for greater representation, inclusion and leadership opportunities for women across the energy value chain. Beyond the glamour, elegant conversations and celebrations, the event carried a clear message: it is time to move beyond conversations about inclusion and focus on measurable progress. The Honourable Minister of Women Affairs and Social Development, Hajia Imaan Sulaiman-Ibrahim , delivered the special address, ably represented by Dr Adedayo Benjamins-Laniyi , Director-General/Chief Executive Officer of the Maryam Babangida National Centre for Women Development . In her address, WIEN President Eyono Fatayi-Williams emphasised that progress must be visible, measurable and sustained. “As we celebrate six years, we also have to ask ourselves an important question: What do the next six years look like? Because we cannot spend the next six years having the same conversations we have had in the last six years. We cannot continue to talk about inclusion without asking what has changed,” Fatayi-Williams challenged the industry. The evening also featured a keynote address by Dr Mutiu Sunmonu (CON) , Chairman of The Sage Centre for Leadership Excellence, who shared perspectives on leadership and the importance of creating opportunities for women to contribute meaningfully to the sector. However, progress is not parity; we are ultimately aiming for true parity. We must acknowledge that most leadership positions today are occupied by men, meaning we cannot achieve our objectives without partnering with them to create access. Whenever I went to work, he would come to pick me up from the office, and we would go home together. In many ways, he looked out for me and made sure I got home safely. We started talking more. We would discuss life, share experiences and occasionally open up about things happening in our individual lives. There was also an emotional dimension to our friendship. Was I considerate? Did I treat him well? Could I have done something differently? I caught myself wondering whether I should have given him a chance . Perhaps I should have allowed him to love me. But then would I have done that out of genuine affection or simply out of pity? And would that have been fair to either of us? My understanding is that not returning someone’s romantic feelings does not mean we cannot offer them genuine friendship, kindness and compassion. I didn’t owe him romantic love, but I could have been a good friend. That has stayed with me. entertainment.description: Report identifies next SME digitization opportunity: connecting payments with day-to-day business management. 94% of SMEs surveyed find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, yet only 29% currently use one, pointing to untapped demand for tools that connect payments with business management. Integrated payment and business solutions can give financial institutions a more holistic view of SME cash flow and support more tailored financing solutions over time. Small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria have largely moved beyond the first stage of digital payment adoption, but a productivity gap remains. According to Visa’s new survey for its Pay and Get Paid 2026 report, most of the SMEs surveyed in Nigeria use digital payments, showing how firmly digital commerce has taken root in the country’s small business economy. However, many SMEs still manage the related financial and operational tasks separately, with only 29% currently using an integrated solution that connects payments with broader business management. The report shows that financial admin and disconnected tools create friction for SMEs, with surveyed businesses citing challenges in tracking outstanding invoices (14%), keeping payroll records organized (19%), and preparing financial reports (16%). These pain points reflect a disconnect between payments and the operational tasks that follow, with some businesses juggling multiple systems to keep their business running. The appetite for a more connected approach is clear. According to the report, 94% of SMEs find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, reflecting strong interest in tools that can bring payments and key business operations into one experience. However, adoption has yet to catch up: only 29% of SMEs currently use an integrated payment and business platform. The report points to several perception barriers that may be slowing adoption. Businesses cited that they already have manual processes that work (8%), that an integrated platform may disrupt their current way of working (8%), or that they do not trust relying on a single provider (7%). These findings suggest that broader adoption will depend on helping SMEs better understand how integrated tools can be relevant, accessible, and scalable for businesses at different stages of growth. At the same time, the experience of SMEs already using integrated solutions suggests a strong value case. The report found that Nigerian businesses using an integrated tool or platform report 93% satisfaction, with 88% reporting efficiency gains, including reductions in the time and effort required to manage their business. In June 2023, ahead of the 66th Grammy Awards, the Recording Academy announced the creation of the Best African Music Performance category. Its creation was a recognition of how far African music had travelled globally, and Nigerian artists were at the centre of that movement. From Burna Boy ‘s Ye , CKay ‘s Love Nwantiti , Wizkid ‘s explosive Essence , to Rema ‘s globally successful Calm Down and others, Nigerian artists became drivers of African music’s global expansion. Afrobeats – the umbrella term often used internationally to describe much of contemporary African popular music, although many Nigerian artists have rejected it for its tendency to limit the range of music coming out of the country – became an established genre globally. While Nigerian and African music have always travelled beyond their respective countries, the era of streaming and digital platforms has accelerated how quickly global audiences discover and engage with the music. African music became increasingly established in the West and other parts of the world, creating greater recognition for its artists and sounds. The Grammys’ decision to introduce a category specifically recognising African music performances was an important step in that direction, beyond the recognition African artists had previously received in categories such as Best Global Music Album. Although the creation of the Best African Music Performance category was celebrated throughout the continent, there seems to be a monopoly, or something close to it, of Nigerian music in the category. While South African artist Tyla has won the award twice, more than any individual Nigerian artist, Nigerian artists have consistently enjoyed greater representation in the nominations. Indeed, Nigerian artists are considerably more recognised globally, particularly in the West. However, I believe it is the responsibility of an award of this repute to look beyond the most visible names and recognise the best African music released within its eligibility period. sports.title: GB's Davis Cup-winning captain ends 17-year stint
sports.description: Leon Smith guided Great Britain to their first Davis Cup title in 79 years [Getty Images] Great Britain's Davis Cup-winning captain Leon Smith is stepping down after almost 17 years in the role. Smith guided the British men's team to Davis Cup victory in 2015 - the nation's first win in the event since 1936. The 50-year-old Scot will leave his role after next week's Finals in Bologna, where he is hoping to create "another special memory" by leading the team to the title once again. Smith's successor has not yet been appointed, but the Lawn Tennis Association (LTA) has spoken to potential candidates and hopes to announce the new captain as soon as possible. Former world number one Andy Murray, who was instrumental in Britain's 2015 victory, is not believed to be interested in the role at this time. "It has been an enormous privilege to lead the team for so many years, and I feel now is the right time, both for me personally and for the team moving forwards," Smith said. "Winning the Davis Cup in 2015 will always be one of the proudest moments of my career, but there are countless other experiences and memories that I'll cherish forever." With Smith picking the team and creating a tight bond between the group, Murray was the driving force on the court as he won all eight of his singles matches in the victorious campaign. Murray was coached by Smith as a child and said winning the Davis Cup together was "one of the proudest moments" of his career. "He did a great job of bringing everyone together and making sure we all felt we had a part to play. He got the best out of us that year," three-time Grand Slam champion Murray said. "I've obviously known Leon a long time, I think the most fun we had together was when I was playing Davis Cup and Leon was on the bench. I'm really glad we got to share those moments. "I wish Leon all the best as he steps down, and good luck to the new captain." sports.description: Behind back-to-back blowout losses and losing Drake Maye to injury , the New England Patriots season has quickly derailed over the last two weeks. Now, they have plenty questions to answers after a much needed bye week. So, let’s get into some of those in this week’s edition of the #PostPulpit Mailbag. What has gone so wrong with the defense? They’re relatively healthy and have a lot of the same personnel as last year. Kuhr did a great job last year and really earned the official promotion to DC. So what happened? Here’s how we’d break them down: Zone coverage: Statistically, the Patriots are the worst zone coverage team in football, ranking dead last in both EPA and passer rating allowed in zone coverage. Defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr was a step ahead of opposing offenses earlier this season with his disguises in the secondary, but teams have caught on while New England’s defensive backs have failed to live up to their potential. Some of the issues in zone coverage also tie back to the pass rush. The Patriots rank 20th in the league in four-man pressure rate, giving opposing quarterbacks time to find the voids in coverage. To generate pressure, New England has had to blitz, which then leaves more space for the offense to attack with at least one defender taken out of coverage — as seen on Jahmyr Gibbs’ 50-yard reception last week. sports.title: Shannon Sharpe thinks he knows ‘the main reason’ why LeBron James left the Lakers
sports.description: Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images LeBron James left the Los Angeles Lakers in the summer of 2026 after eight years with the franchise. The 41-year-old joined the Philadelphia 76ers in the off-season, and he seems to be having a great time there. The Lakers are doing well without him too. Since his summer move, there have been several theories about why James decided to leave the Lakers. Shannon Sharpe has now had his say on what he thinks happened. Shannon Sharpe says LeBron James left the Lakers because he was disrespected James has been one of the biggest names in the NBA for a long time, and when he joined the Los Angeles Lakers, many expected them to dominate. However, the Lakers won just one NBA Championship with The King in his eight years there, which is one of the reasons why things turned a bit sour in the end. Some fans wanted James gone because they believed that Luka Doncic was their real star and would take them to the next level on his own. Sharpe believes that was one of the reasons why James felt disrespected and decided to leave. He said on the Nightcap show : “I think the main reason LeBron left the Lakers is that he felt like they didn’t respect him anymore. “He felt like, ‘Look, I understand Luka’s better, but y’all just blatantly disregarded what I’ve done for you guys the last eight years. Do y’all not remember what transpired the last couple of years Kobe was here? “‘Because Kobe was hurt a lot, and do you remember when Kobe retired, that 60-point game? What y’all did in ’16 and ’17. Do y’all remember that? And then for you to have this kind of laissez-faire attitude, it’s just like, you know what, y’all don’t really appreciate it.’ “And he heard it: ‘We don’t need LeBron. We don’t want LeBron. We got Luka.'” LeBron James’ summer departure has worked out for everyone There was a big debate in the summer following James’ departure from Los Angeles. Some were of the opinion that the Lakers would struggle this season, while others believed that The King’s new team, the Philadelphia 76ers, would have problems because of him. However, when you look at the records of the two teams, they are pretty similar. Of course, the debate about James and the Lakers will go on until the end of the season and perhaps even beyond that point. However, we think people should just accept that his departure was the best move for all parties involved and move on. sports.title: Ben Shelton completes feat only Rafael Nadal can match this century after latest win at the ATP Finals
sports.description: Ben Shelton broke new ground in his career by reaching the semifinals of the ATP Finals for the first time. After Arthur Fils lost the first set of his third and final group stage match against Alexander Zverev on Thursday, Shelton ‘s spot in the final four was confirmed. The 24-year-old American had beaten Rafael Jodar in straight sets earlier in the day to boost his chances of advancing at the prestigious year-end tournament. Photo by Pascal von Büren/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty Images Ben Shelton matches Rafael Nadal after advancing at the ATP Finals With his triumph, Shelton became the youngest American since Andy Roddick in 2004 to reach the semifinals of the ATP Finals. He also became the first left-hander other than Rafael Nadal to do so this century. Nadal made the semifinals six times and advanced to the championship match twice: in 2010 and 2013. The legendary Spaniard never managed to win the title, however, despite making 11 appearances. Shelton qualified for the ATP Finals for the first time last year, but was knocked out in the round-robin stage. He went winless in his debut campaign, winning just one set throughout the run against Felix Auger-Aliassime. This time around, Shelton has tallied a record of 2-1 in the group stage, having beaten Fils and Jodar but losing to Zverev. The loss to the German was his seventh straight in their head-to-head and first since the US Open final. Photo by Sona Maleterova/Getty Images Ben Shelton’s semifinal opponent at the ATP Finals in Turin After finishing second in the John McEnroe group, Shelton will face the winner of the Ivan Lendl group, Carlos Alcaraz, on Monday. Alcaraz secured his spot atop his group after beating Daniil Medvedev and Frances Tiafoe, both in straight sets. Shelton has faced Alcaraz five times on the ATP Tour and has only come out on top against him once. Shelton’s sole victory in the head-to-head came in the quarterfinals of this year’s US Open, where he emerged victorious in a five-set thriller. Alcaraz has since earned revenge by beating Shelton in the Paris Masters final to extend his lead in the rivalry to 4-1. Their upcoming clash at the ATP Finals will be their third on an indoor hard court.

technology.title: Trump admin still won't let Wi-Fi giant TP-Link sell its latest routers in US
technology.description: TP-Link, which may be the top provider of wireless routers for US homes and small businesses, isn't allowed to sell its latest Wi-Fi routers in the US. The Trump administration imposed a sweeping ban on foreign-made consumer routers in March 2026, and TP-Link hasn't been able to obtain an exemption. The rules prevent the import or sale of all new router models that are manufactured, assembled, designed, or developed outside the US. The Trump administration has control over which router makers receive special permission to import and sell new products through a waiver-review process involving the Federal Communications Commission, the Department of Defense, and the Department of Homeland Security. While some of its competitors have obtained exemptions to the ban, TP-Link appears to be having a hard time making its case to government officials. Its routers approved before the March 2026 ban remain available for sale in the US, but its newly released Wi-Fi 8 routers cannot be imported or sold. Read full article Comments

technology.title: Windows 11 passkey bug cries failure after successful sign-in
technology.description: A Windows 11 passkey bug can leave Android phones announcing that authentication failed even when it succeeded. Microsoft has now released a fix for versions 25H2 and 26H2. The problem occurs when users sign in on a Windows 11 PC using a passkey stored on an Android phone. Scan the QR code, and the Android device might display the message: "Something went wrong. Restart the process on your other device and try again." Except it might not have gone wrong at all. Microsoft's guidance explains: "In cases where authentication completes successfully on the Windows device, the error message on the Android device is not supposed to appear and can be safely ignored." Cross-device authentication lets users sign in on one device using a passkey held on another, without typing a password or copying a verification code. Microsoft says the issue affects operations using Microsoft Authenticator and Google Password Manager, and can occur in Edge or Chrome – not just when signing in through Microsoft Entra ID. Cross-device passkey operations with an iPhone aren't affected. An authentication system that cries failure after a successful sign-in isn't doing much for user confidence. Nor will it endear itself to support teams fielding the resulting tickets. Microsoft has included a fix in KB5132057 , the optional non-security preview update released on November 19 for Windows 11 25H2 and 26H2. Until affected devices are patched, users can ignore the Android error if authentication has completed successfully on the PC. ®

technology.title: Ubuntu Core Desktop targets 28.04 debut, with default status in its sights
technology.description: Canonical is targeting Ubuntu 28.04 LTS for the release of its immutable Core Desktop, with a stretch goal of making it the default download for Ubuntu 30.04. Canonical's VP of engineering, Jon Seager, set out the timetable in his opening keynote at Ubuntu Summit 26.10. Yes, we know, we have heard this before: we reported on his plans last month . But this time, there's the beginning of a release schedule. Seager said that Ubuntu Core is already out there in tens of thousands of IoT devices – which seems like a modest estimate to us, and to him too, as he quickly added "maybe more." Despite some noise a few years ago, though, what's still missing is the desktop version. Seager's slides listed three bullet points: that Core Desktop will be "immutable," "composable," and "attestable." As he put it, they are "taking the whole of the Linux operating system, and cramming the whole thing into snaps." Acknowledging that this is going to be wildly controversial, he said: "This is one for the Redditors." He's right. There is a lot of resistance to snap, and in direct response, advocacy of the Red Hat-backed Flatpak instead – but we have seen almost none that is based on either system's technical merits. Much of that opposition concerns claims of one being more open than the other. We've looked at how both systems work, and our impression is that the implementation of snap is cleaner, simpler, easier to use, and more comprehensible. Snap does depend on systemd, which Flatpak does not – but only for now. Flatpak NG is in development and will also need everyone's favorite init system. Ubuntu Core's immutability is not new technology: even Core 16 is now a decade old. It has supported in-place version upgrades since Core 22. We have reported before that Canonical remains strongly committed to its packaging format, and that commitment seems stronger than ever. Seager continued: "Never has a model like snap confinement been more relevant… we're finally in a position where we can bring this to the desktop." The core idea of an immutable OS is that "much more of the system is not writable at runtime," meaning that it "can't be messed with once the system has booted." He talked about the same three use cases we discussed last month. The "browser-centric machine" is the company's analog to Google ChromeOS, and he said that it's essentially ready now, suggesting that everyone listening probably has a family member whose computer is basically just a way to use a web browser. The second was the dedicated games machine, which we interpret as a response to Valve's SteamOS. This edition, he said, would "boot straight to Steam," with "just enough of a shell to launch games." There's also an immutable "development workstation," and here, he offered the example of developers who need to work on some long-unsupported hardware or software, for whom an immutable OS means that you "can't brick your system by installing some weird old dependencies, unmaintained for 20 years." technology.description: Welcome to Friday and therefore to another edition of On Call , The Register 's reader-contributed tech support column in which we share your tales of cleaning up messes made by clients and colleagues. This week, meet a reader we'll Regomize as "Dennis" who told us he once ran a tech support business in a major US city. "I got a call from a very well-known lawyer's office," he told On Call. "Over the two decades I spent supporting his office, this attorney and I became close friends." The attorney was also a good client because Dennis found himself billing a three-figure sum every month for malware removal that resulted from the lawyer’s – ahem – personal browsing habits. Dennis eventually tired of malware removal and told his client to expect a substantial bill for the iMac he was about to buy as a replacement for his PC. "I told him this would pay for itself in 18 months," Dennis wrote, because he figured it wouldn't get malware all the time. "He actually said, with genuine concern: 'If you do that, you will make less money'." Dennis replied that he aimed to give his clients the best advice, and that on this occasion his counsel was to pay Apple instead of himself! "It took him about five years to stumble across anything that could harm that iMac," Dennis wrote. "When he did, I had no idea what to do: I had never seen an infected Apple product." So he did what all tech support people do: reinstalled the OS and crossed his fingers. Dennis was rewarded when the machine came back to life, with all data and settings intact. "I had given up at least $6,000 in support revenue by solving his problem and I'd do it again," he wrote, before winding up his story by letting us know "I retired five years ago. technology.title: Big Tech's compliance with EU market rules is performative, consumer group says
technology.description: Big Tech has earned a finger-wagging from the European Consumer Organisation (BEUC), which says the industry's compliance with the EU's Digital Markets Act (DMA) still leaves consumers short of meaningful choice. BEUC said : "Big Tech companies Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, ByteDance, Meta and Microsoft (so-called 'gatekeepers') still likely breach the EU's Digital Markets Act (DMA) far too often for consumers to reap the full benefits of real choice over their digital services and products." The European Commission designated the six companies as gatekeepers in 2023 , imposing obligations on specified core platform services such as search engines, messaging services, and app stores. The DMA aims to make digital markets fairer and more open to competition. The devil is in the details. In the years since, the EC has lined up Amazon and Microsoft's cloud businesses for gatekeeper status. In March 2025, the Commission issued preliminary findings against Alphabet over Search and Google Play, while separately specifying measures Apple had to take to meet its interoperability obligations. In 2024, Microsoft's browser rivals argued that Edge should also be covered by the DMA's gatekeeper obligations, and so on. Mast points out that both of those companies are on the Department of War’s List of Chinese Military Companies , the designation it uses for entities deemed to be a “military-civil fusion contributor to the Chinese defense industrial base.” That’s a polite way of saying that Washington thinks China relies on these companies to operate and improve its military, and therefore to challenge America’s national security. technology.description: If you’ve got a moment to spare in between sorting out emergency patches for PHP , Java , and PostgreSQL , VMware has just bid for any remaining space on your schedule by publishing two critical-rated security advisories. VMSA-2026-0009 addresses CVE-2026-123890 , a 9.8-rated flaw that VMware says means a malicious actor with network access to vCenter may exploit this issue to bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access to the system. vCenter is the tool admins use to manage fleets of virtual machines. The flaw is present in VMware’s flagship Cloud Foundation suite. VMware also wants its users to address CVE-2026-123891, which allows attackers to read and write the database used by SDDC Manager, the tool for managing entire software-defined datacenters. Attackers can execute arbitrary commands and elevate privileges to root. The prospect of an unknown party getting access to vCenter or SDDC manager is not pleasant. At least VMware has fixed its software. The virty giant hasn't done the same to address a second advisory, VMSA-2026-0010 , which warns that Cloud Foundation, Aria Operations, and VCF Operations HCX products all use Apache – which has a 9.8-rated remote code execution vulnerability (CVE-2026-119618). VMware plans to ship new versions of its products with a patched version of Apache, but for now only has workarounds that disable the http2 protocol. A KVM curiosity Admins who oversee virtual infrastructure also need to pay attention to Linux KVM, the subject of a curious incident over the last 24 hours. This mess started with the November 18 disclosure of CVE-2026-99312 , a bug which allows an attacker to use a guest virtual machine to inflict Denial of Service (DoS) or memory corruption attacks on the host. It’s bad news whenever someone with access to a guest VM can attack the host, because it means gaining access to a single tenant can potentially harm all the other guest VMs or peer into the memory a guest uses. This flaw, however, isn’t a worst-case scenario guest-host escape, because it only impacts users of AMD processors who employ nested virtualization – the practice of running a hypervisor inside a virtual machine. Nested virtualization isn’t commonly used in the enterprise, but clouds employ it to do things like powering OS emulators. The bug’s CVSSv3 score is therefore a modest 5.5. Security researcher Oren Tomtov of Accomplish.ai says the flaw meant he could access 127 GB of host RAM on a Digital Ocean “Droplet” – the junior cloud’s name for its cloudy VMs. Yomtov says he told Digital Ocean and the Linux kernel security team about the flaw in October. "Our usage took a 20x jump yesterday from our Android launch ," co-founder Tessa Brown, a communications scholar and former Stanford lecturer, told The Register in an interview. "Android has been really exciting for us because not only is it 70 percent of the global mobile market, but we rolled out on iOS first. People were so excited to use Germ for their end-to-end encrypted Bluesky DMs, but half of their friends couldn't talk to them." Building a new messaging platform isn't easy, much less one with credible end-to-end encryption. Co-founder Mark Xue hails from Apple, where he worked as a privacy engineer on systems like iMessage and FaceTime. "At the core level, the end-to-end encryption is built on a standardized encryption and Messaging Layer Security," Xue said. "The premise of Messaging Layer Security was to be as good as Signal and deployable by many, many different parties in different applications, which we're taking advantage of to extend the reach of that encryption." Xue said the app is built with its own transport protocol to minimize the amount of message metadata, adding that while the team hasn't gotten around to a formal security audit, it's a step they're considering. Germ Network's goal, said Brown, is to give people more confidence when they communicate. "We do that by giving you more tools to protect your identity, to control what you're sharing with whom," she explained. Instead of using a person's phone number as an identity key, Germ allows users to create cards which represent distinct identities on the network. "Instead of sharing your number, you share a card," Brown explained. "You can build multiple cards; they're not mutually discoverable. Visa’s systems were not involved and were not impacted. No payments data such as card numbers were affected. This is unrelated to any of the system disruptions across different industries this past week.” Mastercard also cited a third-party provider in an email sent to The Register following our questions about the alleged breach. “We were recently informed of an incident at a third-party provider that resulted in the exposure of a limited amount of email addresses - non-payments information - from a small subset of cardholders enrolled in a specific benefit program,” Mastercard SVP Seth Eisen said. “There is no impact to the Mastercard payment network or the ability for people to use their cards. None of the three financial firms would comment on who the third-party providers are, when the breaches occurred, and what specific data was stolen. science.title: Einstein was right! Scientists verify 1st image of a black hole ever captured
science.description: null An independent team of researchers has validated the first image of a supermassive black hole captured by humanity. That, in turn, verifies Einstein's greatest theory, general relativity , which first predicted the existence of black holes and what their immediate surroundings would look like. Captured by a global network of telescopes forming an interferometer called the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) and revealed to the public in 2019, the image shows the supermassive black hole at the heart of the galaxy Messier 87 (M87), located 55 million light-years away. The image of this black hole , designated M87*, with a mass around 6.5 billion times that of the sun, was an immense scientific achievement. That may lead to the question: why did it need verifying at all? Team leader and researcher with Australia's Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation (CSIRO), Samuel Lai explained why capturing the image of a distant black hole is so tricky. "It is like standing in your backyard and trying to take a photo of a doughnut on the moon," Lai said in a statement sent to Space.com via email. Lai and his small Australian team developed advanced machine learning and artificial intelligence techniques to capture information about the black hole's structure and filter out interference resulting from the fact that the EHT was viewing M87* from within our planet's atmosphere. The machine-learning technique called GenDIReCT also accounted for biases introduced by combining telescopes to create an Earth-sized interferometer. "When we applied it to the original EHT dataset, we found a black hole almost identical in size and shape as the historic EHT image. Importantly, our model had no idea what a black hole looked like when we applied it to the M87 data," Lai continued. "This is the first truly independent validation of the EHT image, an important step in the scientific process." This could settle the questions of just how the final image of M87* was influenced by both atmospheric effects and the processing methods needed to reconstruct pictures from telescope data. That's not just good news for the EHT; it's good news for Einstein. Take it away Einstein Einstein published his theory of general relativity in 1915, completely reshaping how we think of gravity. General relativity suggested that objects with mass curve the very fabric of space and time, united as a single entity called spacetime. Gravity arises from that curvature. The greater the mass, the more extreme the curvature and thus the greater the gravitational influence of that object. Taking this to its extreme, scientist Karl Schwarzschild came up with a solution to the equations of general relativity that suggested an infinitesimal region with infinite mass, resulting in unrestrained curvature, a singularity. The robotic Dragon capsule will undock from the International Space Station (ISS) today at around 12:05 p.m. EST (1705 GMT), if all goes according to plan. You can watch Dragon's departure live here at Space.com, courtesy of NASA. Coverage will begin at 11:45 a.m. EST (1645 GMT). A SpaceX Dragon spacecraft supporting the company's 34th commercial resupply services mission for NASA departs the International Space Station on June 16, 2026. (Image credit: NASA/Jessica Meir) If Dragon does indeed leave the ISS today, it will splash down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of California on Saturday (Nov. 21) at about 4:55 p.m. EST (2155 GMT). There will be no livestream for its reentry and splashdown. A safe return to Earth requires relatively calm seas, so NASA and SpaceX are keeping a close eye on the weather in the splashdown zone. If conditions aren't great for a Saturday afternoon return, Dragon will stay docked to the ISS for a bit longer, until things improve. This particular Dragon launched Oct. 13, on a mission called CRS-35 because it's the 35th that SpaceX has flown for NASA's Commercial Resupply Services program. Dragon is the only cargo craft flying today that's capable of making such downward deliveries. science.title: The BepiColombo spacecraft is finally entering orbit around Mercury
science.description: Artist’s impression of BepiColombo orbiting Mercury ESA/ATG medialab After a long and ponderous journey, the BepiColombo spacecraft will finally enter Mercury’s orbit on 21 November. Over the course of the next year, it will investigate the planet’s geology, its tenuous atmosphere and its magnetic field in an effort to understand how it formed and evolved over time. BepiColombo , a joint mission of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA), launched in October 2018. Mercury’s proximity to the sun makes it incredibly difficult to reach without overshooting the planet and falling into the sun, so the spacecraft had to take a long and looping path over the past eight years, flying past both Venus and Mercury several times and using their gravity to make subtle tweaks to its trajectory. In 2024, an issue with the thrusters lengthened that journey even further, pushing the arrival date back from 2025 to 2026. Now, it has finally arrived. Read more 6 of the most fascinating moments in the life of our solar system While it is arriving at Mercury as a single spacecraft, BepiColombo actually comprises two separate orbiters: ESA’s Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) and JAXA’s Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO, or Mio). In December, the two will split apart and move to different orbits – MPO on a near-circular path that takes 2.3 hours to complete an orbit, and Mio on a more distant elliptical orbit, where it will take 9.3 hours to circle Mercury. Advertisement Those split orbits complement the differing scientific objectives of the two spacecraft. MPO is more than twice the size of MMO, and its 11 scientific instruments focus largely on studying Mercury itself . Its instruments include several types of spectrometer to measure the makeup of the surface, a laser altimeter to map its terrain and instruments to study the makeup of Mercury’s extremely thin atmosphere, called an exosphere. Mio’s more distant orbit will allow it to study a broader area around Mercury. It has five sets of scientific instruments to study the magnetic field and atmosphere of the planet, as well as the solar wind that blows strongly in the area close to the sun. Free newsletter Sign up to Launchpad Sign up to newsletter Now that the BepiColombo spacecraft are entering orbit, their primary mission is expected to last only one Earth year, which is a little more than four Mercury years. The mission could potentially be extended for another year, but beyond that the combination of limited fuel and extreme temperatures will make it all but impossible to keep going. Over the course of the year, researchers hope that BepiColombo will provide enough data to solve some of Mercury’s many mysteries. Mercury’s magnetic field is bewildering, because it originates 400 kilometres above the planet’s centre and should have faded away long ago. Its atmosphere must be continuously supplied with material from the surface, but we are unsure exactly how that occurs.

On November 15, 2026 , the Fiji Meteorological Service began issuing updates about a slow-moving tropical disturbance northeast of Samoa and the Cook Islands. Within just a few days, it had become one of the most intense November tropical cyclones the region has seen in decades. Named Xavier , the system intensified rapidly , thriving in an environment with minimal wind shear and sea surface temperatures of 29 degrees Celsius (84 degrees Fahrenheit)—well above the threshold required to sustain and strengthen developing tropical cyclones . Xavier was the basin’s second named storm of the season, following only Wati , a short-lived storm that emerged in October. As Xavier developed, NASA satellite data showed the storm churning along the southwestern edge of a massive tongue of warm water spanning from the west coast of South America to the central Pacific—a telltale sign of the El Niño that has been present in the region since June . When the MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer) on NASA’s Aqua satellite captured this image at 02:53 Universal Time on November 17, 2026 (4:53 p.m. Cook Islands Time on November 16), forecasters estimated Xavier had maximum winds of about 195 kilometers (120 miles) per hour. Winds reached a peak intensity of 220 kilometers (140 miles) per hour later that day, a Category 5 storm on the cyclone intensity scale used in the region or a Category 4 on the Saffir-Simpson scale . The storm ranks as the strongest November tropical cyclone east of the international date line on record, noted Colorado State University hurricane expert Phil Klotzbach . Xavier’s formation east of the date line, near the northern Cook Islands, was unusual, but its easterly position aligns with research that indicates that storm activity in the region typically shifts northeast during El Niño years. Research also shows that El Niño tends to fuel storms that strengthen at an unusually rapid pace . According to news reports, Xavier damaged homes and caused power disruptions as it passed the northern Cook Islands. It then encountered dry air and a less favorable wind shear environment and slowly weakened as it pushed westward, reducing the threat that it posed to Samoa and American Samoa. science.title: Voyager 1 team, unbowed by communications glitch, celebrates epic 1-light-day distance milestone
science.description: null PASADENA, Calif. – NASA's Voyager mission team cheered and wiped away tears here on Thursday (Nov. 19), celebrating a big milestone — Voyager 1 just reached one light-day from Earth , something no other spacecraft has ever done. The excitement persisted despite a communication anomaly that cropped up on the probe, which the team remains confident is temporary. Voyager team members gathered for a press conference about the mission at the Von Karman auditorium here at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) — the first such Voyager event since 1989, when Voyager 1's twin, Voyager 2 , flew past Neptune. The gathering served to celebrate Voyager 1 's distance milestone: At 5:16 a.m. EST (1016 GMT) on Wednesday (Nov. 18), the probe reached one light-day from Earth — the distance a photon travels in one day, which is about 16 billion miles (26 billion kilometers). That means it now takes a full day for a signal to travel from Earth to Voyager 1, the farthest human-made object out in space. "I remember in 1977 I was standing at the Cape watching Voyager launch, and I never thought I would be here today, 49 years later, to celebrate Voyager's one light-day. science.description: null A new set of slo-mo videos gives us a new perspective on SpaceX's first-ever recovery of a Starship upper stage. The company notched the milestone on Saturday (Nov. 14), when the launch tower at its Starbase site in South Texas caught Starship's Ship spacecraft with its "chopstick" arms. You've probably seen photos and videos showing the epic snag from afar. But on Tuesday (Nov. 17), SpaceX released up-close views — a series of four slo-mo videos captured by cameras near the top of the 480-foot-tall (146 meters) tower. The Ship upper stage of SpaceX's Starship megarocket comes back to its launch tower for a "chopsticks" catch on Nov. 14, 2026, during the vehicle's 15th test flight. (Image credit: SpaceX) "The Starbase tower chopsticks catching their first Starship. This unique architecture was designed for full and rapid reusability, enabling repeat launches and landings from the same pad," SpaceX wrote in a Tuesday X post that shared the videos, a compilation of which you can see embedded above. Starship is the biggest and most powerful rocket ever built. Its current "V3" version stands about 408 feet (124 m) tall, and future iterations will be even larger . As SpaceX noted in Tuesday's post, the megarocket is also designed to be fully and rapidly reusable — a first for an orbital launch system. The company plans to catch both Starship stages — Ship and the Super Heavy booster — at the launch tower, a recovery strategy designed to enable efficient inspection, refurbishment and reflight. Another view of the chopsticks catch on Nov. 14. (Image credit: SpaceX) SpaceX planned to carry out such a double catch on this most recent test flight , Starship's 15th to date, which launched on Friday evening (Nov. 13). But Super Heavy experienced a low-fuel warning during its return to Starbase about 6.5 minutes after launch and autonomously diverted to splash down in the Gulf of Mexico. That wasn't a huge deal for SpaceX, as it had already caught Super Heavy on three previous test flights . Snagging Ship is tougher; the upper stage returns to Earth from orbit, so it comes in faster and hotter than the booster does. SpaceX had not even attempted a Ship catch before Flight 15. But the company managed to pull off the maneuver on its first try. And Ship did some work in orbit before coming home: It deployed 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink V3 broadband satellites on Flight 15, the second batch that the company has sent to low Earth orbit . The first set was deployed on Flight 14 , which launched on Sept. 28.

The veteran Hayabusa2 spacecraft launched back in 2014 to collect material from the asteroid Ryugu . Since delivering the samples to Earth in December 2020 via a reentry capsule, the main spacecraft has been conducting an extended mission of exploration and in July made a super-close flyby of the two-headed asteroid Torifune. But Hayabusa2's continued adventures are now set for a premature end. The spacecraft was scheduled to rendezvous with, and attempt to land on, the tiny, 36-foot-wide (11 meters) near-Earth asteroid 1998 KY26 in 2031, but trouble with the aging spacecraft's engines has forced a change of plan.
